b: Algebraic & Geometric Duality of \(\mathbb{C}\): Every complex number \(z = x + iy\) corresponds bijectively to a point \((x, y)\) in the Argand plane with modulus \(r = |z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) and principal argument \(\theta = \arg(z) \in (-\pi, \pi]\). In exponential Euler form, \(z = re^{i\theta} = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\), multiplication scales moduli and adds arguments: \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2 e^{i(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}\).
